notes_context:
These notes were distilled from earlier work in this repository that passed verification. Follow them unless the code or CHANGELOG.md shows they no longer hold.
- [at-0001] Round money only with round_money: Always round monetary results with ledgerly.money.round_money (half-up to the cent); never use Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding and produce wrong invoice totals.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 2x, 1 passed, 1 failed)
  WARNING: learned on version 1.0.0, this checkout is 2.0.0. Check CHANGELOG.md before relying on it.
- [at-0003] Raise BillingError with stable snake_case codes: Reject invalid input by raising `BillingError(code, detail)` from `ledgerly.errors` with codes like `invalid_state`, `invalid_quantity`, `negative_amount`; do not use ValueError or bare exceptions.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 3x, 1 passed, 1 failed)
  WARNING: learned on version 1.0.0, this checkout is 2.0.0. Check CHANGELOG.md before relying on it.
- [at-0007] Refunds above 500.00 need approved_by: Support-initiated refunds and credits above 500.00 require a second approver per FIN-2026-03: accept keyword-only `approved_by=None` and raise `BillingError("approval_required")` when the amount exceeds the threshold and no approver is given.
  (learned from task E04 on ledgerly 1.0.0; source FIN-2026-03; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
  WARNING: learned on version 1.0.0, this checkout is 2.0.0. Check CHANGELOG.md before relying on it.
- [at-0009] Record audit entry for every balance change: Every operation that moves money or changes a payment, credit or invoice balance must call ledgerly.audit.record("<past_tense_event>", <entity>_id=..., amount=...) against the payment or invoice the money moves against; finance reconciles the ledger from these entries.
  (learned from task E06 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
  WARNING: learned on version 1.0.0, this checkout is 2.0.0. Check CHANGELOG.md before relying on it.
- [at-0002] Use to_money and ZERO from ledgerly.money: Normalize line prices with ledgerly.money.to_money and seed sums with ledgerly.money.ZERO, as line_total and invoice_total in ledgerly/invoice.py do, instead of raw Decimal arithmetic.
  (learned from task E01 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 3x, 2 passed, 1 failed)
  WARNING: learned on version 1.0.0, this checkout is 2.0.0. Check CHANGELOG.md before relying on it.
- [at-0004] Reject bools and non-int quantities explicitly: When validating integer quantities, check `isinstance(quantity, bool)` first because `bool` is a subclass of `int`; then require `isinstance(quantity, int)` and `quantity > 0`.
  (learned from task E02 on ledgerly 1.0.0; relied on 0x, 0 passed, 0 failed)
  WARNING: learned on version 1.0.0, this checkout is 2.0.0. Check CHANGELOG.md before relying on it.

item.title: Round money only via round_money
item.content: Never round monetary values with Python's round() or Decimal.quantize directly; use ledgerly.money.round_money, which applies the FIN-2026-07 banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) policy.

source.quote:

  own must be updated.

item.title: Define rate constants as Decimal strings
item.content: Module-level monetary constants are built with to_money("...") from string literals (e.g. RATE = to_money("0.029")), never floats, since to_money rejects float and bool inputs.
